title: Malformed audio chunks are skipped with synchronous recursion
reasoning: When decoding or buffer creation fails, the catch handler calls playNext() directly. If the queue contains many malformed chunks, each failure recurses synchronously before the stack unwinds because atob/createBuffer errors happen before source.start schedules any async boundary. A burst of bad chunks can therefore overflow the call stack and leave playback state inconsistent instead of draining safely.
reproduction: Enqueue a large number of chunks with invalid base64 or invalid PCM byte length while playback is idle; each failed chunk enters the catch path and calls playNext() synchronously until the stack limit is hit.
recommendation: Schedule the next skip on a microtask or loop through failed chunks iteratively, and ensure isPlaying/activeSource are reset if draining aborts unexpectedly.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for PlayerService error-drain behavior, and the package test scripts only show a Jest harness without linked coverage for this service.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Jest test that mocks window.atob to throw for many queued chunks and verifies enqueueAudio drains without throwing RangeError/stack overflow and ends with getIsPlaying() false.
minimumFixScope: Change the catch path in PlayerService.playNext so failed chunks advance asynchronously or via an iterative drain, then add focused PlayerService tests.
